findings.text: Publishes reference tracker directories for inspection through a debug filesystem hierarchy with separate helpers for the primary file and a human readable alias, keyed by tracker identity.

Offers reference count helpers that conditionally decrement only in selected states and combined helpers that acquire a caller supplied synchronization primitive only when the count reaches the last reference.

Exposes lightweight ownership queries that report whether the table wide mutex or a specific bucket lock is currently held, with a permissive answer when debugging support is disabled and a special allowance for nested tables.

Initializes reference tracker debug support in two stages with an early stage preparing background cleanup and index structures and a later stage creating the top level directory, plus background workers that reclaim dead entries and drive table resizing.

Provides a boot time comparison of region allocation strategies that exercises several capacities, measures allocation and release durations separately, validates that each structure ends empty with matching region counts, and requests a retry status so repeated runs do not require unload.

Tracker debug publication is idempotent and ordered: repeat publication for the same tracker is a no operation, alias creation requires a prior primary entry, overlong names prevent creation while keeping prior state, failed index insertion removes the just created filesystem object, and replacement of an existing index entry triggers a one time warning.

Saturation is sticky and diagnostic: once a saturation event is reported the counter is pinned to a saturated value and a one time warning classifies the cause among overflow with leak, operation on zero indicating use after free, decrement to zero indicating leak, or unknown.

Conditional decrement follows a three way contract where an already saturated counter reports success without change, a value of one reports that the caller holds the last reference without changing it in one variant and atomically moves to zero in another, and other values decrement with wrap detection treated as misuse.

Combined decrement and lock helpers avoid locking on the fast path when more than one reference remains, otherwise they acquire the caller lock and revalidate under protection, releasing the lock and reporting failure when another thread changed the outcome.

Benchmark inputs are randomized per capacity with region lengths bounded by a small maximum and capacity fraction, each strategy allocates sequentially until exhaustion then releases in reverse order with timing split between phases, memory accounting is exact for one strategy and a lower bound for the others, and zero capacity is rejected.

Table sizing uses power of two growth with shrink targeting roughly one and a half times the element count clamped to a configured minimum, refusing to shrink when already small enough or when a resize is already pending, and allocation prefers a flat zeroed table with per table randomness and null terminated buckets.

Resizing proceeds through a single future table that immediately receives insertions while lookups and deletions consult both tables, after which each old bucket chain is migrated entry by entry using the new hash, the new table is published, readers are waited upon before deferred release, and a chained future causes another cycle.

Lookup and insertion enforce bounded chain search with configurable strictness, returning distinct signals for duplicate, missing, contended chain, oversized table, and transient resize states, redirecting to the newest table when a resize is in flight and scheduling background work when growth pressure or allocation shortage is observed.

Table mutation paths declare a requirement to hold the table wide mutex in debug builds through a check that is compiled out when lock verification is unavailable, keeping release behavior unchanged while catching misuse during development.
Entry hashing for migration reuses the same policy driven helper as normal operation so that relocation decisions remain consistent with lookup placement.

Retired tables support two release paths with one acting immediately in constrained contexts and another acting after a grace period for readers, where nested levels receive additional cleanup before the outer structure is freed.

Resize requests raised from constrained contexts only schedule process context work, and failed or incomplete background cycles re schedule the same process context work rather than the interrupt level request so that teardown ordering cannot leave a stray request firing after destruction.

Tracker indexes use interrupt safe atomic operations for lookup insertion and removal with deferred filesystem removal on a worker that repeats until no dead mark remains, while table resize paths serialize allocation and attach under a table wide mutex and mutate individual chains under per bucket locks with walker state protected by a separate spin lock and publication ordered for readers.

A nested table is a union of either a pointer to another level or a pointer to a locked bucket head with read copy update qualification, and observed table state includes size and nesting depth, bucket array, pending future link, reclamation callback, walker list, randomness seed, and lock tracking alongside instance counts and policy parameters.
Benchmark scratch state uses three boot only buffers for occupancy, region lengths, and placement results sized from the largest requested capacity and released together on exit.

A tracker filesystem object moves from absent to live on first publication and later from live to dead marked to reclaimed by a looping worker that erases the index before removing the filesystem object, processing alias entries before primary entries each pass.

A hash table cycles among steady, resize pending with a future attached, migrating with per bucket movement, published with old memory awaiting grace period, and re armed for another cycle when growth shrink or nesting pressure remains or when a chained future appeared during publication.

Silent skip on overlong generated names, one time warnings on unexpected index replacement, and reliance on caller provided directory state mean mis sized inputs or concurrent publication can leave inspection entries missing without error propagation.

Reference count misuse is reported but execution continues with a pinned saturated value, and benchmark mismatches in region counts emptiness or expected exhaustion signals are reported as warnings rather than failures, so callers must not treat warning free logs as proof of correctness.

Hash operations distinguish many negative outcomes including contended chains, duplicates, missing keys, oversized growth, busy tables, interrupted attach races, and allocation shortage with some paths automatically scheduling background retry, so callers must handle transient retry signals separately from permanent errors.
Region benchmark uses a maximum region extent of 32 and a default set of 6 capacities forming a decimal ladder from 1000000 down to 10.
Hash table defaults to 64 buckets with a floor of 4.
Tracker debug entries live under a top level directory named ref_tracker with primary files created as owner readable regular files.
